Lemma
[wedge embedding and Ricci adjunction] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0112, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0113 ↗ lem:chow-ii-ricci-contraction-wedge ↗ lem:chow-ii-wedge-satisfies-bianchi 1. ch11:11.15\group Algebraic Curvature Operators If $n>2$, the map $A\mapsto \operatorname {id}\wedge A$ from $S^2(E)$ to $\mathcal A_n$ is injective and is the adjoint of $\operatorname {Rc}:\mathcal A_n\to S^2(E)$.
Proof

\sketch If $\operatorname {id}\wedge A=0$, the scalar trace of 3 gives $(n-1)\operatorname {tr}(A)=0$, and the same formula then gives $(n-2)A/2=0$. For adjunction, expand both inner products in an orthonormal basis and use the curvature symmetries: $\langle \operatorname {id}\wedge A,R\rangle =\tfrac 12R_{ikjk}A_{ij}=\langle A,\operatorname {Rc}(R)\rangle $, with the common normalization induced on the two tensor spaces.

□
